title: Back analysis of mechanical parameters based on GPSO-BP neural network and its application.
summary: For one Zhaotong Tunnel segment, a GA-PSO-optimized back-propagation network inferred rock parameters from displacement inputs; forward calculations matched monitored roof and step displacements with mean relative error 4.34% and outperformed three comparison networks in that case. Generalizability is limited to this field application.
ai_technology: A genetic-algorithm/particle-swarm-optimized back-propagation network inferred four surrounding-rock parameters from displacement monitoring; the estimates were used in forward tunnel calculations.
organization: College of Water Resource and Hydropower, Sichuan University, China; Faculty of Civil Engineering and Mechanics, Kunming University of Science and Technology, China; China Railway Eryuan Engineering Group Co., Ltd, China

evidence.tested: In one Zhaotong Tunnel field segment, forward-predicted roof/step displacements had reported relative errors of 1.11%, -6.88%, -0.41% and -8.97% (mean relative error 4.34%), outperforming BP, PSO-BP and GA-BP in that case.
evidence.unknown: Training used 25 simulation schemes and testing five additional schemes; the field comparison was one tunnel segment. The paper notes limited generalization and weaker cohesion fit.
evidence.ai_role: The learned inversion model supported a field-case parameter estimate checked against monitored tunnel displacement.

source_review.scope: Primary Scientific Reports full text and PMC copy, including field application and parameter-validation Results; publication date checked.
